summary.headline: Glenmark Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue flat at INR473 million reported, but like-for-like growth near 20%; H1 cash flow negative on INR520 million litigation payouts and field force build-out.
summary.overview: Reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations was INR473 million versus INR469 million a year ago, with like-for-like growth close to 20%, while H1 like-for-like growth was about 18%. India formulations grew about 14% like-for-like in Q2 and outgrew the IPM (16.7% vs 13.8%), and emerging markets rose 73.2% YoY to INR8,769 million. North America core growth was about 31% ex the ISB 2001 out-licensing income, with four launches in the quarter. Management said the H1 margin dip reflects front-loaded oncology field force hiring (about 1,100 people) and litigation settlements, and expects operating leverage in H2; gross debt is guided to zero by end FY27.

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR13,274 million, +16.7% vs IPM +13.8% (IQVIA); MAT Sep growth 15.7% vs IPM 12.1%. Ranked 13th with 2.4% share, 11 brands in IPM top 300; ranked 2nd in dermatology, 3rd respiratory, 4th cardiac.

segments.name: Glenmark Consumer Care (GCCL)
segments.commentary: Q2 primary sales INR1,252 million, +46.5% YoY, led by Candid, La Shield, Scalpe, Bontress and Episoft.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR10,089 million; core growth about 31% ex ISB 2001 income. Launched sugammadex injection, fluticasone nasal spray Rx and nintedanib capsule; Flovent 44 generic sole-supplier with about 22% share per IQVIA. Fulvestrant relaunched from Monroe injectable site.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR7,920 million, +6.2%; Western Europe strong, CEE softer. Management expects generics to grow low single digit; growth to come from branded respiratory and dermatology (RYALTRIS, WINLEVI).

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR8,769 million, +73.2%; Russia led by dermatology (ranked 6th), LATAM driven by Brazil, Mexico, Colombia; RYALTRIS launched in Brazil. Management guides 15-20% EM growth consistently.

segments.name: Innovation (IGI and partnered assets)
segments.commentary: IGI R&D about INR187 crore in Q2. ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001) has more than 170 subjects dosed in TRIgnite; updated data at ASH 2026. RYALTRIS sales about $130-140 million annualised, growing 30-40%.

guidance_outlook: Gross debt to be zero by end of FY27 as operating leverage kicks in during H2.
H2 cash generation expected at INR400-800 crore, taking cash to about INR1,200 crore without debt by year-end.
Margin to improve YoY in percentage terms in H2 as H1 field force and oncology investments yield results.

Oncology launches (aumolertinib, trastuzumab rezetecan, envafolimab) to contribute about $30-40 million in FY28, with FY30 $100-150 million and peak $400-500 million by 2035-36 excluding ISB 2001; oncology EBITDA margin about 30-40%.
Aumolertinib first commercial launch expected in H2 FY27; Monroe to add three to four injectable products next year.
Most large US litigation settled; smaller settlements may continue over quarters and years.
capex_capacity: Q2 capex INR262.1 crore (tangible about INR170 crore, intangible about INR92 crore); H1 capex about INR337 crore.
Goa plant received USFDA EIR in Q2; Monroe injectable facility received EIR and fulvestrant relaunched in Q1 FY27, with more Monroe launches planned.
Filed ANDAs for Flovent 110 and generic ipratropium MDI; Flovent 110 and ipratropium launches expected toward end of FY27; one or two more respiratory filings this year.
Field force expansion of about 1,100 people across India and emerging markets in oncology, hired in H1.
demand_pricing: RYALTRIS: marketing applications in more than 90 countries, commercialised in 58, ten more launches expected over next few quarters; sales growing 30-40%, more than 40% YoY in H1; US sales about $15-20 million this year.
WINLEVI: UK formulary coverage 40% of market; launched in Nordics, CEE and Spain; under review in South Africa.
Flovent 44 generic (180-day CGT exclusivity) is sole generic; fluticasone nasal spray approved in September and rolling out.
Glenmark litigation: USD15.3 million Humana settlement (in two instalments) booked; antitrust class action consolidated in Eastern District of Pennsylvania.
Estradiol vaginal pessaries showing strong uptake in US; about 20-plus oral contraceptive products.

qa_highlights.question: How much more US litigation charge visibility is there after H1 provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most big cases are settled; only small amounts are expected going forward, over quarters and years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Flovent headroom and Monroe filing timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Flovent 44 is the sole generic and performing as expected; fluticasone nasal spray commercialisation is starting, with Flovent 110 and ipratropium launches toward year-end. Three to four Monroe injectable products expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: How will EBITDA margin trajectory look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a YoY percentage margin improvement, with H2 benefits from the front-loaded H1 field force and oncology investments; oncology products expected to lift margins from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 operating cash flow negative?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR520 crore of litigation payments, INR337 crore capex, plus interest, dividends and working capital; H2 cash generation expected at INR400-800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross and net debt at end-September?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt about INR866.5 crore and cash INR1,290 crore, giving net cash of INR424 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin expectations for the oncology products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA will be well ahead of the company average, around 30-40% net margin for the oncology products.

risks_watch: H1 operating cash flow negative; H2 must deliver INR400-800 crore to reach zero gross debt and INR1,200 crore cash by year-end.
Residual US litigation settlements may continue over quarters and years.
European generics expected to grow only low single digit; CEE demand softer.
Geopolitical and supply chain cost pressure across the value chain, per management.
ISB 2001 licensing outside AbbVie's territories not discussed; STAR-0310 rights returned from BioCryst effective 4 November, with partnering under evaluation.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and H2 operating leverage, but guarded on specifics: management declined to share ISB 2001 ASH data or licensing plans and gave no quantified EBITDA margin target beyond a YoY improvement.
key_quotes: Excluding the various one-offs from the last year, as well as looking at our core business P&L, excluding IGI, we delivered a 20% Y-o-Y growth in revenue, along with 21% EBITDA margin in Q2.
As the operating leverage kicks in in H2 FY 2027, we expect gross debt to be zero by end of FY 2027.
I think most of our big cases have been settled, right? Now, going forward, we anticipate there will be some possible small amounts which will go out as we go forward.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides to a YoY percentage margin improvement in H2 as H1 oncology field force (about 1,100 hires) and investments yield results; Q2 core EBITDA margin excl. IGI was 21%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Goa (USFDA EIR in Q2) and Monroe injectable (EIR received, fulvestrant relaunched) are commissioned, with 3-4 more Monroe injectables expected next year, but no quantified capacity additions or capex sizes were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Like-for-like revenue growth was about 20% in Q2 and 18% in H1, India formulations grew about 14%, and emerging markets are guided to 15-20% growth consistently, backed by four NA launches in Q2 and ten more RYALTRIS launches expected.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on H2 operating leverage and H2 cash generation of INR400-800 crore, but gave no revenue or margin guidance numbers that could be raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was negative on about INR520 crore of litigation payouts and INR337 crore capex, and H2 must deliver INR400-800 crore to reach zero gross debt; European generics are guided to only low single-digit growth and management flagged cost pressure.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aumolertinib first commercial launch is expected in H2 FY27, Flovent 110 and generic ipratropium MDI launches are expected toward end FY27, and RYALTRIS has ten more country launches over the next few quarters.

rows.label: Gross debt to zero by end FY27
rows.why: Gross debt was INR866.5 crore and cash INR1,290 crore at Sep 2026, and H2 cash generation of INR400-800 crore is guided to take cash to about INR1,200 crore without debt.

rows.label: Oncology franchise revenue ramp
rows.why: Management guides $30-40 million oncology sales in FY28, rising to $100-150 million by FY30 (excluding ISB 2001), at about 30-40% EBITDA margin.

rows.label: Most large US litigation settled
rows.why: Management says most large US cases are settled and only smaller settlements continue, though H1 litigation payouts were about INR520 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, H2 operating leverage and the debt-free target, but guarded on ISB 2001 data, licensing plans and any quantified margin target; analysts pressed on litigation charge visibility and Flovent headroom.
